messages:
OpsBot: :rotating_light: ALERT: High p99 latency + GPU mem pressure observed in dedicated-prod (gpu-pool-east-1). Autoscaler triggered repeated scale-ups in last 9m. Investigating for potential cascade. PagerDuty notified.
PagerDuty: Paging oncall @Ava_SRE. Incident page: https://pagerduty.example/INC-9082
Ava SRE: I'm on it. digging into metrics -> looking at batch sizes + kv cache hit rates. pinging ML for recent changes. /me grabbing logs
Sam ML: I rolled out batching tweak at 03:45 (reduced max_batch_delay from 20ms -> 8ms to reduce latency on small requests). Did not change cache logic. Could that increase simultaneous in-flight prefixes?
Priya Eng: Possible. Lower batch delay increases rate of new KV cache entries because more partial prefixes get evicted. We're seeing a sharp increase in KV insert ops: ~6x baseline since 03:48.
Ava SRE: Here are the key signals I'm seeing:
- p50->p99 diverging: p50 +10ms, p99 +250ms
- GPU mem usage jump: from 60% -> 94%
- KV cache miss ratio up from 6% -> 38%
- Autoscaler events: 4 scale-ups + 3 scale-downs in 9m (thrash)
Marcus PM: Any customer impact? We have a few D3 customers on that pool.
Ava SRE: We're seeing elevated request errors for long context generation (timeout retries) and rate limited flows for a handful of D3 customers. Not full outage yet but increased latency and some 5xx retries.
Sam ML: Hmm. My change made more frequent smaller batches which increases ephemeral KV entries (short-living prefixes). Combined with LRU eviction and fixed cache size, it can blow out eviction churn.
Priya Eng: When eviction churn goes up, memory churn spikes and some workers rewarm KV cache causing longer generation times -> autoscaler sees higher CPU/GPU and scales. New instances start cold, creating more cache misses -> positive feedback.
Ava SRE: That is the autoscaling feedback loop we feared. Immediate mitigation options:
1) revert batching change (rollback) - high confidence but will affect latency improvements we wanted
2) increase KV cache size temporarily for dedicated-prod - buys time
3) bump HPA cooldowns and avoid immediate scale-downs to stop thrash
4) add aggressive prefix deduping to server-side (quick patch) - higher risk
Which do we want now?
Sam ML: Rollback my change to restore steady-state. I can revert right away.
Priya Eng: I'll apply a hotfix to KV cache config: increase max_entries by 2x and raise eviction grace window to 30s. Also change HPA config: set cooldown 300s and min_replicas +=1 for the pool.
Ava SRE: Sounds good. Steps:
- Sam: revert batching change (done ASAP)
- Priya: patch KV config + HPA tweaks (apply as transient ops)
- I'll hold scale actions manual for 10m and monitor
Sam ML: Reverted commit 9f3b2a. Deploy started: `kubectl rollout restart deploy/redwood-inference-batcher -n dedicated-prod`.
OpsBot: Deploy started: rollout/redwood-inference-batcher (uid: deploy-87a1). Status: in_progress
Priya Eng: Patching config now:
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
data:
  kv.max_entries: "2000000" # 2x
  kv.eviction_grace_secs: "30"
---
# HPA patch
spec:
  behavior:
    scaleDown:
      stabilizationWindowSeconds: 300
  minReplicas: 4
```
Applying via `kubectl apply -f kv-hotfix.yaml -n dedicated-prod` and `kubectl patch hpa/infra-pool -p '...'`
Ava SRE: I'm holding auto-scale (temporarily) for the targeted pool via override: `auto-scale: disabled` on infra-manager for 10m. Manual ops only. Monitoring dashboards.
Sam ML: Batch deploy completed. Batch service pod logs show batch delay metrics back to baseline.
Priya Eng: KV config applied. HPA patched. Waiting for pods to rewarm.
Ava SRE: Early telemetry (1m): kv miss ratio falling from 38% -> 12%, p99 dropping ~120ms. GPU mem usage trending down.
Marcus PM: Customer impact update: notified affected D3 customers with preliminary note. No escalations yet. Keep me posted.
Priya Eng: Noted one worker OOM in the middle of the blowup, killed by Kube. We've increased pod memory requests on the pool to prevent immediate OOMs during rewarm.
Ava SRE: Good call. Watch for thrash: if we see more than 2 scale events in 10m after re-enable, we will keep HPA disabled and do manual ramp.
OpsBot: Incident Silence: alerts suppressed for dedicated-prod pool for 10m by Ava SRE.
Sam ML: Observability note: we should add a delta metric for "kv_insert_rate / kv_eviction_rate" to surface churn early.
Priya Eng: Agreed. Also adding warmup hook: when a new replica spins up, it should check replicated cache snapshot before accepting traffic. Low-risk change.
Ava SRE: For now, actions summary (on-call):
- Incident severity: P2 (degraded performance for subset customers)
- Mitigations applied: revert batching change, increase KV size, HPA cooldowns, increase pod mem requests, manual scale hold
- Customer impact: elevated latency/5xx for D3 customers; communications sent
- Next steps: add cache warmup snapshot, add churn alert, re-evaluate batching config in staging with KV churn sim
- Ownership: Priya Eng (hotfix + follow-up), Sam ML (batched config revert + testing), Ava SRE (oncall coordination and RCA)
Marcus PM: Thanks. Please prepare blameless postmortem draft with timeline and mitigating actions. Highlight tradeoffs on latency vs cache stability.
Ava SRE: On-call handoff: I'm covering for 15 more minutes then handing to Priya for overnight; Priya, you taking second shift?
Priya Eng: I can take handoff and will watch dashboards for next 3 hours. Ping me @Priya_Eng if anything spikes.
Ava SRE: Handoff notes:
- active mitigations in place
- don't re-enable autoscale until kv miss ratio < 8% for 15m and no scale events
- if p99 spikes > 300ms re-escalate to SRE rotation
Priya Eng: Got it. Will follow up with config PRs for warmup and churn metrics tomorrow morning.
Ava SRE: Closing the live thread for now; will update incident channel with final RCA later. :wave:
OpsBot: Incident update logged: INC-9082 - P2 - KV cache churn + batching regression -> autoscale thrash. Timeline saved.
